I was in Cloquet today at Community Memorial Hospital to talk about my plan to make health care more affordable and accessible – and to strengthen the community hospitals that are there for Minnesotans when they need them most.

That means lowering costs, protecting access, and expanding our health care workforce so Minnesotans can get the care they need when they need it.
posts.summary: Advocates lowering healthcare costs and strengthening community hospitals

posts.text:
My opponent calls Trump’s health care cuts “good for Minnesota.” And when Trump refused to extend the premium tax credits, she stood by and did nothing. 

As Governor, I’ll take action to bring down prescription drug costs and give Minnesotans relief from rising premiums. 

Minnesotans deserve a Governor who does what’s right for them – not what’s right for a Wisconsin billionaire donor and Donald Trump.
posts.summary: Opposes Trump health care cuts, promises to lower drug costs and premiums

posts.text:
Retired nurse Tom Smart worked at Winona Health as a nurse for 20 years. 
He went from provider to patient in an instant when he had a heart attack. When every second counts, he was able to turn to care right in his community: Winona Health.

But Trump’s cuts are putting hospitals like Winona at risk. That puts lives at risk, too.
As your Governor, I will fight to keep your health care close to home.

posts.text: One size doesn’t fit all when it comes to health care in Minnesota. Yesterday I was at Community Memorial in Cloquet with their CEO Rick Breuer, talking health care workforce, affordability, and access. Their ROSE Program trains rural providers to safely handle emergency childbirths — exactly what we need to do to expand health care access in Minnesota.

posts.text:
We need to lower health care costs, which have skyrocketed across the country.

My opponent supported the Big Beautiful Bill’s drastic Medicaid cuts and doesn’t support extending the health care tax credits to give Minnesotans relief from rising premiums.

If the Trump administration won’t act, as Governor I’ll create a state tax credit to bring these costs down.
